_comment: The closed enum of suite commands the trusted measure job may invoke. This file is authority: it lives
beside the workflow, on protected main, and is checked out by SHA. The candidate never contributes a
command - not through a dispatch input, not through its package.json, not through a file in its own tree.
A dispatch may only pick a KEY from this table; the command text is whatever this file says it is.
_timeout_comment: WHY EVERY COMMAND CARRIES --test-timeout, AND WHERE THE NUMBER COMES FROM.
Without it a single hung test consumes the whole job. The measure job is bounded at 20 minutes and the
suite it runs takes about five, so one test that never settles spends the remaining fifteen producing
nothing, and the job ends as a CANCELLATION - which carries no diagnostic naming what hung, which leaves
no capture to look at, and which the emitter can only refuse downstream as `measure_job.conclusion`
without ever being able to say why. A review reproduced exactly that hang on this repository's own
coordinator suite under an unusual TMPDIR. The job bound is the outer limit and it stays; this is the
inner one, and what it buys is that a hang becomes a NAMED cancelled point inside a complete capture,
with every other file of the suite still measured.
600000 ms, AND THE FIRST NUMBER TRIED WAS WRONG, which is why this paragraph states the measurement
rather than the intention. `--test-timeout` in node 22 bounds EVERY test, and a test file is itself a
test whose duration is the whole file's run - so the flag is a per-FILE bound as much as a per-test one.
Chosen from the slowest single test point of the pinned candidate's real capture (32.4s), 120000 looked
like 3.7x headroom; run for real it killed two whole files at 120s and the measurement came back with
3538 tests instead of 3667, 2 cancelled points, and 129 tests that never ran. Measured properly, the two
files are 273s and 176s standalone - the 273s file is the critical path of a suite whose whole wall clock
is 300s - so the smallest honest value is one that clears the slowest FILE, not the slowest test.
600000 is 2.2x the slowest file measured standalone and 2x its in-suite worst case, and it is half the
measure job's own 20-minute bound.
THE DIRECTION THE ERROR RUNS, stated because this flag can turn a green suite red: a test - or a file -
that legitimately needs more than 600s now FAILS, and a failing point that a term names means that term
establishes nothing. That is the safe direction for an authority whose only job is to refuse what it
cannot vouch for, but it is a real cost. Re-derive the number from a measured run if a runner key is ever
added, or if this suite grows a slower file - and never raise it to accommodate a hang.
WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY: the bound is 600s against a job bound of 1200s, so a hung test still costs half the
job. Node offers no per-test bound that is not also a per-file bound, so tightening this further means
splitting the suite across runner keys, not lowering this number.
